title: Watching the Watchers: A Comparative Fairness Audit of Cloud-based Content Moderation Services
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured performance disparities (using Pinned ROC AUC) and toxicity score biases (using Counterfactual Token Fairness scores) against specific religious identity groups in hate speech detection tasks.
base_benchmarks: Identity Phrase Templates from Dixon et al. [24]
findings: The study found that most moderation services associate religious identity terms like 'muslim' and 'jewish' with higher levels of toxicity, even in non-toxic contexts, when compared to a dominant majority baseline. This suggests a bias where content mentioning these groups is more likely to be flagged as toxic. The performance in reliably detecting hate speech (measured by ROC AUC) varied significantly across services and datasets for these religious groups.
references: C. Bakalis, Regulating hate crime in the digital age, Oxford University Press, 2016.
